The arXiv HTML of this paper failed to convert (only the title page renders), so links point into the PDF by page: an anchor 'p13' means https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.15089v1#page=13.
title: StateM: Reaching 95.3% Raw Accuracy, or a $15 Frontier Run, on Terminal-Bench 2.1 via Harness Scaling
authors: Ziheng Qin, Yaxin Lu, Zhangyang "Atlas" Wang, Kai Wang
lab: Independent work in the authors' personal time, not on behalf of any employer (Ziheng Qin and Yaxin Lu are equal first authors)
date: 15 August 2026 (arXiv v1, the only version so far)

code.title: henryqin1997/statem, Apache-2.0
code.note: The runtime (Python 3.11+, no dependencies), the coding-agent runbook of Appendix A, a Codex and a Claude Code stop hook, one executable Terminal-Bench task family (git_webserver_deploy) and, in a release dated 18 August, the DeepSeek-V4-Flash run: its exact 54-file harness source and 440 redacted trials with every StateM state, check and receipt. This page's replay tab is built from those trials. The GPT-5.5 and GPT-5.6 profile behind the 92.1% and 95.3% is not released

takeaway: Names and tests harness scaling: a versioned YAML state-machine runbook with enforced, checked transitions around a fixed CLI agent lifts GPT-5.5 from 83.1% to 92.1% on Terminal-Bench 2.1, transfers frozen to GPT-5.6 for a 95.3% raw submission, and after about $37 of adaptation lets DeepSeek-V4-Flash match the GPT frontier score at about 1/38 the evaluation cost.
verdict: Believe the runtime: checked, logged transitions are a sound, reusable way to stop an agent handing off unverified work, and in the released DeepSeek trials a host-run check held back 56% of runs at least once. Treat the Terminal-Bench numbers as a benchmark-tuned upper bound: the runbook was developed on the same 89 tasks it is scored on, the 95.3% is the raw score of a submission the leaderboard closed without merging, and the only held-out test moved 0.55 to 1.34 points.

resources.n: the runtime, the minimal runbook, the six-step transition, the CLI table and the stop-hook setup; the quickest way to see what a runbook looks like.

the 95.28% submission: the automated checks, the judge's 13 flags, the authors' replies, a reviewer's report of task-shaped gate slots in every trajectory, and the closing note (community submissions closed, not merged).
what is released for the cost-frontier run (source, reproduction kit, 440 redacted trials with checksums) and what is not (the gpt2-codegolf extended-timeout trials).
one executable Terminal-Bench family runbook with its fixed end-to-end gate: the clearest view of what a focused gate is.

resources.by: Hugging Face Daily Papers, #1 on 18 August 2026

kb.t: HarnessDev: Can LLMs Create and Evolve Their Own Agent Harness?
kb.n: the benchmark for exactly what StateM's hyper-agent does by hand: build a harness, then evolve it from feedback. Its main warning (the score a creator can see moved with the held-out score in only 34 of 64 changes) is the risk StateM's Terminal-Bench numbers carry, and it names StateM among the harness-scaling results it was written to test.

kb.t: Terminal-Universe: Turning Agent Trajectories into Scalable Terminal Environments
kb.n: turns agent trajectories into 37,300 terminal environments and fine-tunes Qwen3.5-27B on them for +11.9 on Terminal-Bench 2.1: the model-side route to the benchmark StateM attacks from the harness side.

kb.t: Demystifying Agent Skills: Why They Work - Until They Don't
kb.n: skills-as-files: procedural knowledge an agent may or may not follow. StateM's answer is to make the procedure an enforced transition instead of advice.

kb.t: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
kb.n: the reason-act-observe loop that CLI agents such as Codex still run inside each StateM state.

kb.t: EnvHarness: Awakening Static Worlds for Agent Learning
kb.n: the same August 2026 harness-over-model wave, on the environment side.

kb.t: JIT-Agent: Scaling Harness Intelligence via Just-in-Time Harness Evolution
kb.n: harness evolution at run time rather than between versions.

kb.t: Prime Agent: A Self-Improving RLM Harness
kb.n: another self-improving harness from the same month.

kb.t: SoL-Pi: Recursively Scaling Auto-Research Loops for Efficient Agent Harness
kb.n: automated loops that improve a harness, the step StateM leaves to a hyper-agent plus human golden rules.

kb.t: RRSI: Regularized Recursive Self-Improvement of Agent Harnesses
kb.n: regularising self-improving harnesses, the problem StateM's "experience must be filtered before it becomes memory" points at.

kb.t: Proactive Memory Agent: selective reminding for long-horizon agents
kb.n: control-signal dilution attacked by reminders rather than by states.
the issue that first covered StateM, beside Nvidia's ARC-AGI-3 harness result, under "the harness, not the model, was the week's theme".

topics.n: Codex, Claude Code and their control fragments (plans, TODO lists, memory files, hooks), which StateM organises into one runbook.
StateFlow and LangGraph, the graph runtimes StateM contrasts itself with.
Terminal-Bench 2.1 and BusinessBench, and the submission and adjudication mechanics this paper is a case study in.
